As I've mentioned several times like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110403, Blend never implies starting playback from the beginning.

This was an issue reported in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/41028, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86984, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100009, and the current behavior has been fixed.

Based on the Capture (DiscreteCarry) mode code, Capture (DiscreteCarry) mode forces the time progression of two animations to sync even when sync is disabled.

When sync is enabled, I believe the only difference occurs when blending animations of different lengths.

Upon reconsidering the behavior of Capture (DiscreteCarry) mode, it seems this is merely a remnant from before sync was implemented. Now that sync exists, it may serve little purpose. We should consider deprecating it in 5.0 and migration into sync.

But it seems that the occurrence of errors in Capture mode is simply a bug, so you can send it as a separate issue.

is there any plugin or feature for the usecase for blending starting playback from the start? The game i'm trying to make heavily relies on that and it broke a lot of things when migrating to 4.6

@RafaelGilVelarde If you know the position where BlendPosition changes, it should be possible to seek to 0 at that moment using NodeSeek chained to BlendSpace or the transition self option in a StateMachine that nests BlendSpace. If BlendSpace had a signal like point_changed, it might have been simpler, but it's not implemented yet. Although there's a proposal in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13386.

A possible workaround here, though it might be quite hacky, is to add a custom property like `@export var blend_state: string` to the AnimationTree. Then, have every animation existing on the BlendSpace have as property track, with a unique key for each animation. After that, detect changes to the blend_state and execute the seek.
